note: Eight guards. Items 1-3 are the last three check:rule-guards miscitations in the repo; item 4 is the second of the two static analysers the checker cannot import-check. The tree was quiet and this auditor's alone. No dev server was needed — contrary to the batch brief, all three deep-zoom smokes are node-only pure-CPU and run in ~0.7s each, not browser-based and slow.

guards.kind: node-only, pure CPU. Imports engine/fractal/deepZoom/{referenceOrbit,laBuilder,LAInfoDeep} directly and validates the LA (linear-approximation) construction pipeline against direct perturbed iteration.
guards.baselineNumbers: 3 cases, 9 assertions, exit 0, 0.70s. stages=4 LAs=381 (250,84,42,1) @ maxIter 1000; case B nodes=100 max rel err 7.46e-4; stage-1 avg skip 12.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(1) when failed > 0, implicit 0 otherwise.
guards.break: Five falsifications, each applied and reverted independently. (A) stepLA drops the +1 on CCoeff.re — the classic double-counting bug. (B) stepLA's ZCoeff.re uses + instead of - on the imaginary cross-term (conjugation error). (C) MAX_LA_STAGES=1 in laBuilder — the entire higher-stage tree never builds. (D) every stage-0 LA finalised with StepLength=0. (E) compositeLA's own ZCoeff conjugation, same shape as (B) but on the stage-1+ path.
guards.result: BEFORE REPAIR only (A) was red (exit 1, rel err 7.12e-1 vs 1e-3 bound). (B), (C) and (D) were ALL GREEN, exit 0. (C) printed 'stages=1' and the silent else-branch 'only 1 stage (orbit too short or trivial)'. (D) printed 'nodes=0 max relative error=0.00e+0' and the central assertion passed because maxRelErr initialises to 0. AFTER REPAIR all five red with distinct assertions: (B) 'stepLA 2 ZCoeff = (-20, 40): (44, 40)'; (E) 'compositeLA ZCoeff = (-10, 10): (-2, 18)'; (C) two failures on the stage floors; (D) three failures including the imaginary-Ref floor.
guards.verdict: cannot-fail on a destroyed LA table + real-axis-blind fixtures (repaired)
guards.note: Two distinct diseases in one guard. The vanishing-input pair ((C) and (D)) is the fifth failure mode exactly: the LA acceleration structure — the whole point of the file — could be reduced to nothing and the guard still said yes. The third ((B)) is the batch-4 degenerate-fixture lesson transposed to complex arithmetic: all three cases used centerY: 0, and a real-axis reference orbit makes z2im identically zero, so every imaginary-part sign error in stepLA and compositeLA was unreachable. Measured: 0 of 500 iters have nonzero Z.im at c=(-0.75,0) vs 499 of 500 at the period-3 complex nucleus. Worth recording that the tolerance alone was NOT sufficient even with the complex fixture added — break (B) moved max rel err 2.49e-4 -> 6.83e-4, a genuine 2.7x signal that the 1e-3 bound still absorbed. That is why case D asserts exact equality on hand-computed values instead. Separately measured and documented, not changed: the 1e-3 bound sits only ~1.34x above the real-axis measurement of 7.46e-4, while the header comment claims the error should be at the LA threshold scale of 2^-24 ~ 6e-8 — four orders out. Deterministic, so sensitivity rather than flake risk.

guards.kind: node-only, pure CPU. Checks detectPeriod / newtonNucleus against four published minibrot nuclei, plus the computeReferenceOrbit integration that adopts a one-period reference (ADR-0066).
guards.baselineNumbers: 7 cases, 23 assertions, exit 0, 0.69s. All four nuclei refined to <1e-12; deep-zoom integration adopts period 3, orbit length 3, relocated true.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(1) when failed > 0. Does NOT stop at the first failure, so breaks isolate well.
guards.break: Three falsifications, each applied and reverted independently. (F) newtonNucleus steps the wrong way — c = c.add(delta) instead of c.sub(delta). (G) detectPeriod updates the derivative AFTER z instead of before, so d_n uses z_n rather than z_{n-1}. (H) NUCLEUS_MIN_ZOOM raised 1e-6 -> 1e6 in referenceOrbit.ts, opening the gate at every zoom.
guards.result: ALL THREE RED. (F) exit 1, 12 failures across all four nuclei — Newton lands 1.1e-1 to 1.5e-1 away and z_P(c*) no longer ~0. (G) exit 1, "period detected: got 14" on the period-1 cardioid. (H) exit 1, 2 failures — "no period (shallow gated out): period=1" and "full-length orbit kept: length=1", i.e. exactly the two assertions that exist to pin the gate. (H) also went red on smoke:deep-zoom-orbit (2 failures), so the gate is doubly covered.
guards.note: No vanishing-input hole: the four nucleus CASES are a const literal in the file, there is no external corpus to go missing, and the null-Newton path counts a failure rather than skipping (if (!cStar) { check(false); continue; }). Both halves of the zoom gate are pinned — one case asserts it engages at depth, one asserts it does NOT at zoom 1 — which is why break (H) produced a two-sided failure instead of a silent behaviour change. The fixtures are published constants to 16 digits, so none of them is arithmetically degenerate. No change made.

guards.kind: node-only, pure CPU. Runs computeReferenceOrbit on nine known-good cases — zero orbit, fast escape, bounded boundary point, precision selection at 1e-30, power=3, and two Julia configurations.
citedBy: .claude/rules/navigation.md mentions it only to say it is unrelated to camera orbit
guards.baselineNumbers: 9 cases, 27 assertions, exit 0, 0.71s. 64 bits at zoom 1, 146 bits at 1e-30; 10000 iters built in 34ms.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(1) when failed > 0.
guards.break: Three falsifications, each applied and reverted independently. (I) HPComplex.sqr returns a2.add(b2) instead of a2.sub(b2) — the core complex-squaring identity. (J) choosePrecisionBits drops the fromZoom term, so precision no longer tracks depth. (H) the NUCLEUS_MIN_ZOOM gate flip, shared with the nucleus guard.
guards.result: ALL THREE RED. (I) exit 1, but on exactly ONE assertion — "Z[1] = z0^2 + c ~ (-0.35, 0.72)" in case I. (J) exit 1, isolating cleanly on "precision bits >= 100: got 64". (H) exit 1, 2 failures — "all 50 iters" and "all 1000 iters computed", because the gate relocated the reference to a one-period orbit.
guards.verdict: healthy, with a measured thinness on complex arithmetic
guards.note: Detects all three breaks, so not blind — but worth recording exactly how narrow one of those margins is. Cases A through H are all real-axis or start from z=0, where a2-b2 and a2+b2 agree because b=0. The ONLY assertion in the file that can see a complex-squaring error is case I Z[1], one iteration deep, and it exists precisely because a prior author added a Julia case with a nonzero z0 imaginary part. Same disease as smoke:deep-zoom-la had, caught here by a single line rather than missed. Not repaired: the guard does go red, and unlike the la smoke there was no green break to justify surgery. Flagged so a future session does not delete case I as redundant with case H — case H starts at z0=(0,0) and proves nothing about squaring.

guards.kind: STATIC ANALYSER — reads files as text, so check:rule-guards cannot import-check it and explicitly asks for the scan paths to be verified by hand. Compares the repo snapshot of the MB3D decompiler against a canonical copy OUTSIDE the repo at H:/GMT/stuff/mb3d-decomp/.
guards.baselineNumbers: 4 files, all IN SYNC, exit 0. Canonical dir present on this box (31 files); repo snapshot has 12.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct: exit 1 on any drift or missing-in-canonical. But exit 0 when the canonical dir is absent — documented as the other-box case, and confirmed by pointing MB3D_DECOMP_CANONICAL at a nonexistent path (warning printed, exit 0).
guards.break: Five falsifications. (K) append a line to a GUARDED repo file (decompile.mjs). (M) append a line to an UNGUARDED shared file (detect-loops.mjs). (M2) same, to gen-sample-scenes.mjs, after adding it to FILES. (N) convert a guarded file to CRLF. (O) move a guarded repo file aside. Plus a by-hand diff of every file present in both trees.
guards.result: (K) RED exit 1 naming decompile.mjs, before and after repair. (M) GREEN exit 0 — the allowlist gap. (M2) RED exit 1 after repair. (N) before repair would have been a false DRIFTED; after repair reports "IN SYNC (line endings differ only)" exit 0. (O) before repair an unhandled readFileSync ENOENT; after, a clean "MISSING in repo" exit 1. The by-hand diff found gen-sample-scenes.mjs differing today — repo 3566 bytes CRLF vs canonical 3511 LF, i.e. exactly its 55 line endings and no content change.
guards.verdict: allowlist blind spot + latent false-red (both repaired)
guards.note: The check:zindex precedent held exactly: an allowlist that omits the files that matter. gen-sample-scenes.mjs regenerates the COMMITTED engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/sampleScenes.ts (verified tracked with git ls-files), so it is the same class as generate-library.mjs and its omission meant drift there would silently revert shipped output — the precise regression this guard was written after, twice. The second defect is subtler and was why the first could not be fixed alone: core.autocrlf=true is set and nothing in .gitattributes covered this directory, so a plain git checkout rewrites these files CRLF against an LF canonical and a byte-exact compare would call all five DRIFTED with identical content, while the remedy it prints would not survive the next checkout. gen-sample-scenes.mjs was already in that state. The repo had already solved this exact problem once — debug/compat-snapshot.jsonl carries a text eol=lf pin with a comment naming the same failure for test:compat — so the fix is the established pattern, not an invention. Left unchanged deliberately: exit 0 when the canonical dir is missing. It is the documented cross-machine contract and narrowing it is a judgement call; the header now says a skip warning means NOT CHECKED, never in sync.

guards.kind: node-only. Byte-exact decode gate for the MB3D parameter-block parser: a 100k synthetic codec round-trip, two gold blocks with externally-published values, and a 5-fixture structural sweep.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(1) when fails.length > 0.
guards.break: Four falsifications of engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/parseMB3D.ts. (P) width reads header offset 8 (height’s slot) instead of 4. (P3) the mirror — height reads offset 4. (Q) codec quad packing shift 12 -> 11. (R) addon formulaCount reads a+5 instead of a+4.
guards.result: BEFORE REPAIR (P) was GREEN, 24 passed / 0 failed, exit 0. (Q) RED, 11 passed / 18 failed including 98436 codec round-trip mismatches. (R) RED, 22 passed / 6 failed. AFTER REPAIR both (P) and (P3) RED at exit 1 with the dims printed — [840x840 x5] and [1400x1400 x5] respectively.
guards.note: Both gold blocks are SQUARE — arcimboldo 5680x5680, asymmetric 5000x5000 — so the only assertions that check dimensions exactly cannot distinguish the width and height offsets. The five digitalstew fixtures are non-square at 1400x840, but the sweep predicate only tested h.width > 0 && h.height > 0. Same class as the freqStart: 0 tautology in test:migrations, with two equal fields standing in for the zero. No vanishing-input hole: fixtures are read by hardcoded filename through readFileSync, so a missing one throws rather than yielding an empty green run.

guards.kind: node-only, 1667 lines. Covers the MB3D weave path end to end: weaveSequencer, the modulo/block/counts schedulers, rhythm conversion, emitWeave assembly, emitFusedHybrid, the native slot catalog and resolver, and legacy-scene migration.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(1) when fails.length > 0.
guards.break: Three falsifications, each applied and reverted independently. (S) buildBlockPlan in schedule.ts drops the silent-step marker on negative counts (seq.push(r) instead of c < 0 ? ~r : r). (T) emitFusedHybrid drops the last slot from the ledger. (U) getNativeSlotCatalog truncated to one entry per category.
guards.result: ALL THREE RED. (S) exit 1, 323 passed / 1 failed. (T) exit 1, 321 passed / 3 failed — and test:mb3d stayed green under the same break, correctly, since the parser harness does not touch the emitter. (U) exit 1, 323 passed / 1 failed on "P4.3: catalog greys self-contained with reason".
guards.note: Strongest guard of the batch and the only one that already did the anti-vanishing-input thing unprompted: it carries ck("catalog non-empty", all.length >= 70) — an explicit floor on the size of a scanned collection, which is exactly the repair batch 4 had to add by hand to test:shader and test:modulation-coverage. Constructs every fixture in code from directly imported formula defs rather than reading a corpus, so there is nothing to go missing. No change made.

guards.exitContractNote: Correct: an explicit process.exit(1) at each of the four failure points. Success path exits implicitly 0. pageerror is collected and checked, though only after the UI assertions.
guards.break: Three falsifications of engine/plugins/topbar/PauseControls.tsx, each applied and reverted independently. (V) onClick no longer calls setIsPaused. (W) the Slider label renamed from "Auto-Stop (Samples)" to "Sample Limit" — the exact anchor the popover assertion locates. (X) the popover never renders ({false && showMenu && ...}).

(W) and (X) both "sample cap slider visible: false" then "hover popover did not expose the sample cap slider" — (W) proving the anchor is load-bearing, (X) proving the hover mechanism itself is covered.

The popover assertion is only meaningful because a previous auditor fixed it: the header records that it used to read an unscoped document-wide .text-[8px] selector that landed on an unrelated menu badge and was logged rather than asserted, so a completely broken popover passed. guards.baselineNumbers: 2704 pass, 0 fail, 817.2s (13.6 min), exit 0. 52 eligible formulas. Slowest guard in this batch by two orders of magnitude.
guards.exitContractNote: Correct and count-based: process.exit(fail > 0 ? 1 : 0). Output jsonl is gitignored, thumbnails untracked — no tracked artifact written.
guards.break: Three falsifications, each applied and reverted independently. (Z) drop the side-effect import of engine-gmt/formulas/index.ts so the formula registry shrinks. (Y) emitFusedHybrid emits the same GLSL function name for every slot (dropping the per-slot index suffix) — a namespace collision. (AA) append malformed GLSL to each emitted slot body. (Y) and (AA) run with --pair for speed against the full-matrix baseline.
guards.result: ALL THREE RED. (Z) exit 1 with "only 7 eligible formulas — expected at least 52", firing BEFORE any browser work. (Y) exit 1, 0 pass / 1 fail, failing gate webglCompile. (AA) exit 1, 0 pass / 1 fail, same gate.
guards.verdict: healthy — and already carries the shrunk-matrix gate the fifth failure mode calls for
guards.note: The only guard in this batch that already had the anti-vanishing-input protection AND had measured it: FORMULA_FLOOR = 52, with a comment dated 2026-07-29 recording that dropping the formulas barrel import took the sweep from 2704 pairs to 49 while still printing "49 pass 0 fail" and exiting 0. It also names why this matters more here than elsewhere — the matrix is QUADRATIC in the formula count, so losing 5% of formulas loses ~10% of pairs. Falsified that gate directly (break Z); it fires correctly. One footgun found and NOT repaired because the shipped contract is unaffected — see the Tier B finding on the resume path.

Added MIN_NODES_CHECKED and MIN_LA_STAGES floors with the observed values recorded in source (100/167 nodes, 4 stages @ 1000 iters, 6 @ 5000); ran case B a second time on the period-3 complex nucleus c=(-0.1225611668766536, 0.7448617666197442) plus an assertion that the fixture really does carry nonzero Ref.im; converted case C's silent else-branch into a failing check; added case D, exact-equality unit checks on stepLA and compositeLA using hand-computed distinctive values (no component 0, 1 or repeated). findings.verification: Five breaks applied and reverted independently against pristine main. Before: (A) RED, (B)/(C)/(D) GREEN at exit 0. After: all five RED with distinct failing assertions, quoted in the guard entry. Every hardcoded expectation in case D was pre-verified against the live source with a throwaway probe before being written, so the guard cannot be permanently red on a value I got wrong. git diff clean after revert, AUDIT_GS01B5 grep empty, npm run typecheck exit 0, repaired guard green in 0.8s.

findings.summary: Without --fresh, test:weave-sweep exits 0 with "Nothing to do" when every requested pair is already in the results jsonl — a manual --pair run can report success while testing nothing.
findings.rationale: Hit live during this sweep: running the harness with --pair=Mandelbulb,AmazingBox printed "--resume: skipping 1 already-tested pairs" then "Nothing to do (use --fresh to re-run)" and exited 0, having compiled nothing. The npm script passes --fresh, so test:weave-sweep as cited in the rules is NOT affected — the jsonl is wiped every run and FORMULA_FLOOR covers the shrunk-matrix case properly. The exposure is a human or agent running the harness directly with --pair or --primary to check one cell, reading exit 0, and concluding it compiles. Options: (a) leave it — resume is deliberate and the guard as shipped is sound; (b) exit 1 when a resume skips everything, which makes the no-op loud but breaks anyone scripting resume as idempotent; (c) keep exit 0 but print the total-skip as a warning to stderr. Recommend (c) — it removes the silent-success reading without changing any exit contract. Not applied: it is a behaviour change to a documented workflow.

summary.headline: Items 1-3 took check:rule-guards to ZERO for the first time in this audit, and the fix added coverage rather than removing it: the three deep-zoom smokes were healthy but cited on a rule scoping none of the code they touch, while engine/fractal/deepZoom/** was scoped by no rule at all — so they moved to a new deep-zoom.md that closes the orphan. Four of eight guards needed repair. The sharpest finding is smoke:deep-zoom-la, which passed three separate ways on a wrecked LA table, including with every stage-0 node at StepLength 0 while printing "nodes=0 max relative error=0.00e+0" and calling it a match. Second theme, twice over: a fixture whose values make its own assertion degenerate — test:mb3d cannot distinguish the width and height header offsets because both gold blocks are square, and the deep-zoom fixtures were all real-axis, which makes the imaginary term in the LA math unreachable. Third: check:mb3d-decompiler, one of the two analysers the checker cannot import-check, guarded 4 of the 11 files it shares with its canonical copy and was one git checkout from false-redding the four it did. The encouraging half: test:weave-sweep and test:mb3d:weave already carry explicit size floors on their scanned collections, so the fifth failure mode is starting to be designed against rather than only found.
